messages:
Maya Rivera: Heads-up from the Optimize alpha: the regression alert card currently says "Quality dropped" which felt alarmist in user testing. Need softer language + clear next steps.
Carlos Jimenez: Agreed. Users panicked thinking model outputs were corrupt. We want to signal a measurable regression but avoid urgent/irreversible wording.
Ethan Liu: UX goal: be clear about what happened, why it matters, and give two actionable next steps (re-run eval, view failing prompts). Keep primary CTA lightweight.
Maya Rivera: Draft short title: "Model quality decreased on recent evals" Body: "We detected a drop in evaluation score for this model on your alerting suite. Review failing examples or re-run the evaluation to confirm." Primary CTA: "View failures" Secondary: "Re-run eval"
Carlos Jimenez: Slight wording tweak: change "Model quality decreased" -> "Evaluation score decreased" (more precise). Also include magnitude in the body when available: e.g., "down 4.2 points vs. baseline".
Ethan Liu: Good. Also add a one-line explanation of possible causes: "Cause could be a model update, input drift, or config changes." Put that as muted subtext, not the main copy.
Maya Rivera: Accessibility: toast should announce as a polite alert via aria-live="polite". The primary CTA must be a button with aria-label that includes the eval name and model name.
design-bot: Accessibility lint: avoid links that read only "View" or "Details". Include descriptive link text. Ensure focus order goes to the primary action.
Carlos Jimenez: Localization keys suggestion: `alerts.eval.regression.title`, `.body`, `.cta_view_failures`, `.cta_rerun`, `.hint_causes`, `.aria_label_view_failures`
Ethan Liu: Example final copy for translations: Title: "Evaluation score decreased" Body: "This model's evaluation score on '{suite_name}' dropped {delta} vs baseline. Review failing examples or re-run the evaluation to verify." Primary CTA: "View failing examples" (aria-label: "View failing examples for {model_name} on {suite_name}") Secondary CTA: "Re-run evaluation" Hint (muted): "Possible causes: model update, input drift, or config changes."
Maya Rivera: Tone: use single-sentence body, avoid technical jargon like "regression" in user-facing copy. Maybe swap title back to include 'evaluation' but not the word 'regression'. e.g., "Evaluation score decreased" is fine.
Carlos Jimenez: Also propose a compact summary line for the alerts inbox: "{suite_name}: {delta} ↓" so the list is scannable.
Ethan Liu: For devs—add telemetry events: `alert.eval.opened`, `alert.eval.rerun_clicked`, `alert.eval.view_failures_clicked`. Also add a flag to include the `delta` and `model_version` in the event payload.
QA-bot: QA note: when implementing, ensure the failures panel is keyboard-focusable and that the copy is present in the DOM (not only set via image) for localization checks.
Maya Rivera: Final localization-ready snippets to drop into the translations file:
- alerts.eval.regression.title = "Evaluation score decreased"
- alerts.eval.regression.body = "This model's evaluation score on '{suite_name}' dropped {delta} vs baseline. Review failing examples or re-run the evaluation to verify."
- alerts.eval.regression.cta_view_failures = "View failing examples"
- alerts.eval.regression.cta_rerun = "Re-run evaluation"
- alerts.eval.regression.hint_causes = "Possible causes: model update, input drift, or config changes."
- alerts.eval.regression.aria_view_failures = "View failing examples for {model_name} on {suite_name}"
Ethan Liu: I'll wire the aria-label and telemetry. Carlos, can you confirm the UI will display the delta when available and fall back to "a change" when not?
Carlos Jimenez: Yep, delta optional. Fallback copy: "a change in score". I'll add a small inline tooltip on the delta explaining how it's measured.
Maya Rivera: LGTM. Let's keep the primary CTA conservative: users want to inspect before they rerun. Ship copy + aria keys in the PR and QA can test the flows.
Carlos Jimenez: PR incoming with copy + telemetry + delta tooltip.
Maya Rivera: Thanks all :sparkles:
